description:
Find real hills near a location, nearest first (or biggest first with sort_by: gain).
Coverage: the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Switzerland, Austria, Berlin and Brandenburg, California, Oregon, Washington,
British Columbia, Colorado, New York, New Jersey, Massachusetts, the Chicago area, the Tokyo area, Sydney and Cape Town; elsewhere has no climbs.
Only climbs within max_distance_km (default 10) are returned; if there are too few, call again with a larger radius.
Climbs are OpenStreetMap roads and trails (footpaths, tracks, bridleways, steps) with elevation from 1 arc-second terrain data.
Use for hill sprints, hill repeats or hilly runs: a long climb can be used for shorter reps.
For planning a hilly run or matching a race's climbing, use sort_by: gain and a wider max_distance_km, then pass climbs to plan_route.
Each result links to walking directions to the bottom (googleMapsUrl) and to the climb on the vertfinder map (vertfinderUrl);
show each climb to the person as a markdown link to its vertfinderUrl, not as a wayId.
Each result has gap_dist_m, its flat-equivalent length from an approximation of Strava's GAP curve. Give a pace (mm:ss per km or mile)
to get est_ascent_seconds, an estimate of one rep up the climb; with min_minutes/max_minutes it only returns climbs whose ascent fits that range,
e.g. for 3, 6 or 10 minute hill reps. pace_mode gap (default) treats the pace as flat-equivalent effort; pace treats it as the actual uphill pace.

lat.description: latitude; with lon, takes precedence over location

location.description: Postcode, town or place name, searched worldwide: add a region or country (e.g. "Richmond, North Yorkshire, UK") and check the returned location. Required unless lat and lon are given.

lon.description: longitude; with lat, takes precedence over location

max_distance_km.description: only return climbs within this many km, at least 0.1 (default 10)

max_minutes.description: only climbs whose estimated ascent takes at most this many minutes; needs pace

min_gain_m.description: minimum approximate climb gain in metres (default 0)

min_length_m.description: minimum climb length in metres (at least 200 unless steps is set)

min_minutes.description: only climbs whose estimated ascent takes at least this many minutes; needs pace

pace.description: running pace as mm:ss per pace_unit, e.g. 6:00; enables est_ascent_seconds and the minutes filters

pace_mode.description: gap (default: pace is flat-equivalent effort, adjusted for gradient) or pace (actual uphill pace)

pavement.description: only road climbs mapped with a pavement along their whole length; many roads lack pavement data in OpenStreetMap, so this also drops climbs whose pavement is unknown

sort_by.description: distance (nearest first, default) or gain (biggest climbs in the radius first; use for planning hilly routes)

steps.description: only trail climbs that include at least one flight of steps; also includes staircases shorter than 200 m

name: find_climbs
